name: Racehorse Pitch
description: Racehorse Pitch is a Pitch variant where the dealer bids and leads; players race to reach the target (e.g. 21) with bid and trump mechanics as in Pitch. High-Low-Jack-Game scoring. See Pitch for base rules.

overview.description: Racehorse Pitch is a Pitch variant where the dealer bids and leads; players race to reach the target (e.g. 21) with bid and trump mechanics as in Pitch. High-Low-Jack-Game scoring. See Pitch for base rules.

history.origins: Racehorse is a cutthroat (individual-play) money variant of Pitch, documented by Patrick Mathews. Pitch is a North American game derived from the old English All Fours (Seven Up or Old Sledge); the modern form with bidding and setback arose in the mid-19th century. Racehorse is usually played by five or more people, each for themselves; the pitcher pays or receives money per point bid. Origins are US; cutthroat Pitch is often played on the coasts for money.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card French deck, as in base Pitch: four suits, thirteen ranks each (Ace through King). Six cards are dealt to each player.

rules.objective: Reach 21 (or target). Bid; make bid to score. High, Low, Jack, Game.
rules.gameplay: 1. Deal 6 each. 2. Bidding. 3. Pitcher leads; suit = trump. 4. Play tricks. 5. Score: High, Low, Jack, Game. Set = setback.
keyRules: High, Low, Jack, Game. Setback on failed bid.

strategy.basic: As Pitch. Bid with strong trump.

variations.name: Pitch
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Base Pitch rules apply; Racehorse differs in dealer bidding and target only.

scoring.description: 4 pts: High, Low, Jack, Game. Setback if bid failed.
